function: Multiagent DRL (MINT) learns AAV position moves and discrete charging-time fraction; AAV association and STAR-RIS phases come from closed-form Algorithm 1 (Theorem 1), not learned (pp. 6-7, 11).
system: Single-antenna AAVs (2) and devices (8); two simultaneously transmitting-and-reflecting RISs, 10x10 elements; 3 GHz, 1 MHz bandwidth; 100 m x 100 m area (pp. 3, 9).
method: Multiagent DRL (MINT, based on FACMAC): GRU policy network, value network and mixing network; centralized training, decentralized execution; reinforcement learning, 1000 training episodes (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Custom simulation: Rician-fading direct links (Eq. 2, 10 dB factor), LoS AAV-to-STAR-RIS link (Eq. 3), perfect CSI; no 3GPP model or measurements; random device positions (pp. 4, 9).
test_conditions: Training (1000 episodes) and execution (50 episodes) in one simulator; Figs. 5-7 sweep reflecting elements, devices, UAV energy; Fig. 8(a) gives convergence time per device count (pp. 9-11).
baselines: Four variants of MINT with one element changed: C-RIS (conventional RIS), T&R-PR (random STAR-RIS phase), RA (random association), CDTTE (equal charging/data time); no earlier learned method (p. 10).
metrics: Energy-efficiency (bits per joule), number of uploaded bits, cumulative reward, convergence time, execution time (pp. 9-11).
complexity: Execution-phase order O(E_P N(U(2 Xi_i Xi_o + Gamma_i Gamma_h + Gamma_h) + IU + IUSM_bM_c)) (p. 9); measured execution and convergence time versus devices, Fig. 8 (p. 11).
openness: none (no code or data link in the paper, pp. 1-13).
q1_support: p. 4: "modeled as the following Rician fading channel [21]". Custom Rician and LoS models with a 10 dB factor and path-loss factor 2.2 (Table I, p. 9); no 3GPP TR 38.901/38.811, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "Convergence time and execution time versus the number of devices". A convergence time is reported for each device count, so each setting is trained; the paper never states that a trained policy is tested on a configuration not used for training.
q3_support: p. 10: "T&R-Phase Randomized Algorithm (T&R-PR): The T&R phase shifts of STAR-RIS elements are randomly generated." A random-phase non-learned baseline exists, but C-RIS, T&R-PR, RA and CDTTE are variants of MINT; no earlier learned method is compared (IDQN [35] is only cited, p. 7).
q4_support: p. 9: "in the execution phase, the complexity of the MINT algorithm is" O(E_P N(U(2 Xi_i Xi_o + Gamma_i Gamma_h + Gamma_h) + IU + IUSM_bM_c)); Fig. 8(b), p. 11, plots measured execution time.
q5_support: p. 9: "we conduct simulation experiments based on Python 3.9 and Pytorch 1.8.1". Custom simulation (Table I, p. 9); no code or data link and no public channel dataset.
notes: Included as area 6 with a borderline above_phy call: the DRL action holds only the AAV move and the charging-time fraction (p. 6), so a time resource allocation in an aerial link is learned jointly with the trajectory (above PHY). The abstract says STAR-RIS matrices are scheduled, but they come from closed-form Algorithm 1 (Theorem 1, pp. 6-7), so area 3 does not apply. The q3 baselines are MINT variants only; q2 is 0 because no test on an unseen configuration is stated.
